features.name: Free Website Build + Growth Hosting
features.audience: Melbourne and Space Coast businesses that need a clearer site, stronger local visibility, and a dependable lead path
features.promise: See a custom website concept before paying a design fee; approve it, then Growth Hosting keeps the site live and improving for $98 per month.
features: Custom first website concept with no upfront design fee
Hosting, SSL, technical upkeep, local SEO foundations, and performance checks
Weekly local content tied to the services customers actually search for
Lead capture, confirmation, and routing checks before launch

campaign.hook: A free website is only useful when the path after approval is clear.
campaign.summary: A custom concept first; $98/month Growth Hosting starts only after the owner approves launch.
campaign.problem: Owners are often asked to fund a redesign before they can inspect the offer, mobile experience, or lead handoff.
campaign.demonstration: Show the custom concept, mobile first screen, contact path, and launch checklist before asking for approval.
campaign.proof: The owner can review the actual concept before deciding whether Growth Hosting is worth starting.
campaign.metric: Qualified enquiries, completed contact paths, mobile performance, and time to a useful response.
campaign.objection: The first concept has no upfront design fee; the $98 monthly service begins only after owner approval.

features.name: AI Agent Foundation
features.audience: small businesses that want to prove one useful AI workflow before funding a larger build
features.promise: Start with one business task, a secure account, linked source material, and a custom system prompt for $10.
features: One narrow workflow instead of a vague all-purpose chatbot
Secure account setup and basic knowledge-source connection
Custom operating prompt matched to the business task
Human handoff with an integration guide

campaign.hook: $10 should buy a decision, not a mystery chatbot.
campaign.summary: A $10 proof of concept for one narrow AI task, approved sources, and a human handoff.
campaign.problem: Small teams can overfund broad AI projects before proving that one narrow workflow is useful.
campaign.demonstration: Show the exact task, approved source material, operating prompt, answer, and human handoff in one flow.
campaign.proof: A scoped proof of concept makes the useful behavior and the missing production work inspectable.
campaign.metric: Correct task completions, escalations, source coverage, and unresolved exceptions.
campaign.objection: This is a focused proof of concept, not a finished enterprise deployment or an all-purpose employee.

features.name: White-Glove Onboarding
features.audience: owners who need a working AI and lead-capture system without becoming their own implementation team
features.promise: EB28 configures the agent, knowledge base, lead capture, and tool connections, then hands over a working system with a human owner.
features: AI agent and knowledge base configured on approved business data
Lead capture connected to the site, inbox, and CRM
One-to-one kickoff and operating handoff
Thirty days of measured adjustments after launch

campaign.hook: The setup is part of the product.
campaign.summary: EB28 configures the agent, knowledge, lead capture, tool connections, and the first 30 days of adjustments.
campaign.problem: Owners do not need another empty dashboard and a folder of instructions they have no time to implement.
campaign.demonstration: Map the configured agent, approved knowledge, lead capture, connected tools, human owner, and recovery path.
campaign.proof: The handoff includes a working system, named ownership, and a measured adjustment period instead of setup promises alone.
campaign.metric: Successful handoffs, unresolved exceptions, routing accuracy, and corrections during the first 30 days.
campaign.objection: EB28 configures the system, while the business keeps its accounts, data boundaries, and consequential decisions.

features.name: Private AI + Local RAG
features.audience: teams that need useful answers from private documents without pasting sensitive material into public tools
features.promise: Run a focused AI workflow on local hardware or a controlled cloud path, with approved retrieval sources and accountable review.
features: Local or controlled-cloud model deployment
Semantic search across approved company documents
Role-based access and explicit data boundaries
Cited answers, human review, and logged corrections

campaign.hook: Private AI starts with what the model is not allowed to see.
campaign.summary: A focused AI workflow on local hardware or controlled cloud, using approved sources and cited answers.
campaign.problem: A useful assistant becomes a liability when source boundaries, access, citations, and corrections are undefined.
campaign.demonstration: Diagram approved documents flowing through retrieval into a cited answer, human review, and logged correction.
campaign.proof: Every answer can be tied to an approved source and reviewed by an accountable person.
campaign.metric: Citation coverage, answer corrections, access exceptions, and unresolved questions.
campaign.objection: Private does not mean invisible or unreviewed; it means controlled sources, explicit access, and accountable operation.

features.name: EB28 App Builder
features.audience: founders and operators who need to turn a rough product idea into an inspectable build brief and working source
features.promise: Start with a short prompt, expand it into a real creative brief, compare distinct directions, and inspect the generated source.
features: Prompt expansion into audience, goal, capabilities, and design fundamentals
Reference-screenshot direction for tone, spacing, and color mood
Three distinct visual directions for side-by-side review
Live preview, source inspection, version history, and ZIP export

campaign.hook: A prettier prompt is not a product brief.
campaign.summary: Turn a rough prompt into a structured brief, three directions, live preview, source, and ZIP export.
campaign.problem: Rough ideas fail when audience, goals, capabilities, states, and visual fundamentals stay implicit.
campaign.demonstration: Show one rough prompt becoming a structured brief, three distinct directions, a live preview, and inspectable source.
campaign.proof: The builder exposes the brief, versions, preview, and generated source so the direction can be evaluated instead of imagined.
campaign.metric: Time to an inspectable prototype, unresolved fundamentals, version comparisons, and export readiness.
campaign.objection: Generated source is a starting artifact to inspect and improve, not automatic proof that a product is production-ready.

features.name: Recon Agent Founder Beta
features.audience: operators who need a daily view of payout and reconciliation problems without digging through every transaction by hand
features.promise: A focused operating summary that surfaces payout problems early and keeps the next review action visible.
features: Daily operating summary
Fast identification of payout and reconciliation problems
Founder onboarding support
A narrow workflow with visible source evidence

campaign.hook: The payout problem should surface before the month-end scramble.
campaign.summary: A daily, evidence-linked view of what matched, what looks wrong, and what needs review next.
campaign.problem: Operators lose review time when matched payouts, exceptions, and the next action are buried across transaction exports.
campaign.demonstration: Show a daily summary separating what matched, what looks wrong, the source evidence, and who reviews it next.
campaign.proof: The workflow keeps the exception and its supporting record visible instead of replacing accounting judgment.
campaign.metric: Unmatched items, time to review, corrected exceptions, and items still waiting on evidence.
campaign.objection: Recon Agent surfaces and organizes review work; it does not move money or replace an accountant.

features.name: Revenue + Lead Automation
features.audience: service businesses that lose qualified enquiries between the first click, the form, and a useful human response
features.promise: Capture intent, acknowledge the lead quickly, preserve source context, and route the next step without automating away judgment.
features: AI-assisted lead qualification with a visible human escalation
Source-aware confirmation, routing, and reminder flows
CRM handoff and lifecycle measurement
Consent, sender identity, opt-out, and recovery checks

campaign.hook: The first five minutes after a qualified enquiry are part of the product.
campaign.summary: Capture intent, confirm quickly, preserve source context, and route a useful human response.
campaign.problem: Qualified buyers disappear when confirmation, context, ownership, and the next response are slow or ambiguous.
campaign.demonstration: Trace one enquiry from source page through confirmation, qualification, routing, CRM handoff, and human reply.
campaign.proof: The system preserves buyer intent and makes failed, duplicate, or unowned handoffs visible.
campaign.metric: Time to useful response, completed handoffs, duplicate messages, failed routes, complaints, and opt-outs.
campaign.objection: Automation supports the relationship; it does not impersonate judgment or remove consent and escalation controls.

features.name: Bluechip Founding Beta
features.audience: retail traders who want an inspectable Robinhood agent with paper-first onboarding and a public activity record
features.promise: A $98 one-time software license for a paper-first equities desk that starts small, keeps every decision visible, and stays under the operator's control.
features: Paper mode against real prices before any live-money decision
Dedicated Robinhood Agentic sub-account controlled by the operator
Public activity tape with wins, losses, and no-trade days
Guided Setup Portal and human onboarding

campaign.hook: Paper mode is the first release gate, not the demo.
campaign.summary: $98 one-time licensed software for a paper-first equities desk with operator-controlled live access.
campaign.problem: Black-box trading software asks for trust before the operator can inspect decisions, stopping conditions, or account boundaries.
campaign.demonstration: Show paper-mode cycles, the dedicated account boundary, a decision journal, the public tape, and the operator-controlled live switch.
campaign.proof: The buyer can inspect activity, inactivity, losses, and system state before making any live-money decision.
campaign.metric: Cycles, reviews, placed decisions, paper fills, system status, and unresolved blockers — never promised returns.
campaign.objection: Bluechip is software, not investment advice; trading carries real risk of loss and the operator remains responsible.

features.name: Desk OS Safety System
features.audience: operators experimenting with autonomous market agents who care more about stopping conditions than hype
features.promise: Eight specialized agents behind one local-first operating system built around control, containment, and review.
features: Global kill switch with every desk off by default
Capital guard and per-desk circuit breakers
Append-only decision journal and public dashboard
Local-first operation on the owner's machine and keys

campaign.summary: Eight specialized agents behind a local-first safety system with one global kill switch.
campaign.problem: An autonomous agent is not operationally ready when nobody can explain what stops it, contains it, or records the exception.
campaign.demonstration: Show the global kill switch, capital guard, per-desk circuit breaker, decision journal, and current lane state.
campaign.proof: Controls and degraded states are visible separately from any trade or performance result.
campaign.metric: Blocked decisions, stopped lanes, journal completeness, capital-guard events, and unresolved safety checks.
campaign.objection: Safety controls reduce avoidable exposure; they do not remove market risk or make autonomous trading safe by default.

features.name: Fund Manager Live Tape
features.audience: buyers who want to inspect what the agents actually did before believing a product claim
features.promise: A public operating record that shows activity, inactivity, errors, wins, and losses in the same place.
features: Live lane and venue status
Recent decisions and position activity
Transparent degraded or no-trade states
A proof surface separate from the checkout page

campaign.hook: A live tape should show nothing happening, too.
campaign.summary: A public record of activity, inactivity, errors, fills, losses, and degraded states.
campaign.problem: A highlight reel hides the no-trade days, errors, degraded lanes, and missing evidence buyers need to evaluate a system.
campaign.demonstration: Open the current tape and show its update time, lane states, recent decisions, inactivity, errors, and fills in context.
campaign.proof: The proof surface is separate from checkout and includes unflattering operating states rather than only selected wins.
campaign.metric: Snapshot freshness, active and degraded lanes, decisions, fills, errors, and unresolved blockers.
campaign.objection: The tape is operating evidence, not a return forecast, audited performance record, or promise of future results.

features.name: Bluechip Setup Portal
features.audience: new beta operators who need to configure the desk without guessing at account, mode, or risk settings
features.promise: A guided path from license to paper mode, with an explicit operator handoff before anything touches real money.
features: Plain-English setup sequence
Paper-mode default and risk-setting review
Dedicated-account guidance
Human onboarding available within the beta flow

campaign.hook: No one should guess their way from a software license to live money.
campaign.summary: A guided path through account boundaries, paper mode, risk settings, and operator review.
campaign.problem: Account selection, mode, credentials, limits, and stopping conditions become dangerous when they are buried in setup assumptions.
campaign.demonstration: Walk through the account boundary, paper-mode default, risk settings, connection checks, and explicit operator handoff.
campaign.proof: Each setup gate stays visible and paper mode remains the default until the operator deliberately completes the required review.
campaign.metric: Completed setup gates, failed connection checks, unresolved risk settings, and paper-mode verification.
campaign.objection: Completing setup does not authorize live trading; the operator must make and own that separate decision.
